title: How Vaccines Train Your Immune System
post_title: How Vaccines Train Your Immune System | QuantaTale
post_description: How a vaccine teaches the body to defend itself and why protection can last, from the CDC and WHO. Sources: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention https://www.cdc.gov/vaccines/basics/explaining-how-vaccines-work.html and World Health Organization https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/vaccines-and-immunization-what-is-vaccination #Science #ScienceFacts #QuantaTale
narration: How can a harmless dose teach your body to beat a disease? Vaccines help the body learn to defend itself without a full-blown infection. The germs in vaccines are killed or weakened, so the vaccine does not cause the disease. Every vaccine has an antigen, which makes the immune system begin producing antibodies. After the threat is gone, white blood cells stop multiplying until only a few remain to keep watch. Your immune system remembers, so you typically stay protected for years, decades or even a lifetime. The World Health Organization estimates that childhood vaccines alone save millions of lives every year. A vaccinated person can still catch an infection, but is much less likely to become seriously ill or die. Some people, such as very young babies, cannot be vaccinated, so they depend on others being vaccinated to stay safe.
